messages.author: 45e4d261cc3d645c
messages.subject: Concordance of multi-word units
parts:
Dear all,

I'm writing a script that will allow me to retrieve concordance for the Dutch substitutive construction "in plaats van" (i.e. "in place of"). Since this construction allows for syntactic manipulation such as interpolation, omission of the last preposition etc., I needed regular expressions to retrieve all the types of that construction. Here follows the lines of code I tried:

#### The following lines will serve to make a concordance of an unannotated text file.

corpus.files.dutch<-choose.files() # open all the corpus files of Dutch texts selected from the Project Gutenberg

all.matches.ipv<-vector() # reserve a data structure for the results

for(i in 1:length(corpus.files.dutch)) {
cat(i, "\n") # output a progress report
current.corpus.file<-scan(corpus.files.dutch[i], what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T) # to access the individual values of the vector since we need the counter
current.matches.ipv<-grep("in (de|mijn|je|jouw|uw|zijn|haar|onze|jullie|hun)? pla[ae]ts (van|der|den)?", current.corpus.file, ignore.case=T, perl=T, value=T)
if(length(current.matches.ipv)==0) { next }
all.matches.ipv<-append(all.matches.ipv, current.matches.ipv)
}

When I run the script in R, it only retrieves matches for the type "in de plaats (van)", when it should also have returned matches for many other types. The regular expression which seems problematic is higlighted.

I thank you in advance for your comments and suggestions!

C. Bechet.

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Concordance of multi-word units
parts:
When I run the following

####################
ccf <- c("Ik heb alleen mijn plicht gedaan,' zeide ik: 'en ieder
fatsoenlijk man zou in mijn plaats evenzoo gehandeld hebben.",

"hij heeft den Geuzenpenning afgedaan en draagt in plaats
daarvan, zeer in het oog vallend, een rozenkrans van gouden kralen en
een rijk versierd kruis.",
"Als hij gemeend heeft dat er een abuis in de opgave des
afstands is, daar het wel drie uren zal zijn in plaats van twee,",
"Wat hij niet tasten kon, het was de stille uitstorting des

gemoeds, die in haar plaats had;")
exact.matches("in (de|mijn|je|jouw|uw|zijn|haar|onze|jullie|hun)?
pla[ae]ts (van|der|den)?",

ccf, case.sens=FALSE)
####################

I get matches in ccf[1] and ccf[4], namely
"in mijn plaats "
and
"in haar plaats "

First, note that you're effectively asking for two spaces:
- at the beginning after in
- before "pla"
which you probably don't want.

Second, what you think should be matched in ccf[2] doesn't get matched
because of "daarvan", which is not in your search expression. Thus,
this works:

####################
exact.matches("in ?(de|mijn|je|jouw|uw|zijn|haar|onze|jullie|hun)?
pla[ae]ts ((daar)?van|der|den)?",
ccf, case.sens=FALSE)
# $`Exact matches`
# [1] "in mijn plaats " "in plaats daarvan" "in plaats van" "in
haar plaats "
# $`Locations of matches (lines)`
# [1] 1 2 3 4
# etc.
####################

HTH,
STG

parts: I've just figured out how to do the same without "exact.matches". With the following line of code, 346 hits (19th C. corpus) and no fewer than 651 hits (20th C. corpus).

corpus.files.dutch<-choose.files() # open all the corpus files of Dutch texts selected from the Project Gutenberg

for(i in 1:length(corpus.files.dutch)) {
  cat(i, "\n") # output a progress report
  current.corpus.file<-scan(corpus.files.dutch[i], what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T) # to access the individual values of the vector since we need the counter
current.matches.ipv<-grep("in ?(de|mijn|je|jouw|uw|zijn|haar|onze|jullie|hun)? ?pla[ae]ts ?(van|der|den)?", current.corpus.file, ignore.case=T, perl=T, value=T)

if(length(current.matches.ipv)==0) { next }
  all.matches.ipv<-append(all.matches.ipv, current.matches.ipv)
}

all.matches.ipv


Now, for people interested in an improvement of the script (e.g., to expand the context of the concordance), I'm going to try, if I can.

parts:
Here follows what I've tried to to to generate a concordance for my Dutch expression.

> corpus.files<-choose.files()
>
> whole.corpus<-vector()
>
> for(i in 1:length(corpus.files)) {
+   current.corpus.file<-scan(corpus.files[i], what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T)
+   current.corpus.file.2<-tolower(current.corpus.file)
+   whole.corpus<-append(whole.corpus, current.corpus.file.2)
+ }

> matches.ipv<-grep("\\bin ?(\\w{2,10})? ?pla[ae]?tse? ?(hiervan|daarvan|van|der|den|dien)?", whole.corpus, ignore.case=T, value=T, perl=T)

> head(matches.ipv)
[1] "quam in zyn plaats."
[2] "zo wierd richold offe in odolfs plaats verkooren, en is 1ste koning"
[3] "ridzert aurundulus in zyne plaats, die zyn kindskind was."
[4] "goede erkentenisse mogen houden. in zyn plaats quam bonifaas, als"
[5] "eenigen tyd, quam weder een andere in zyn plaats."
[6] "inboorlingen uit den frieschen adel, tot landvoogden stelde, in plaats"

> output.file<-choose.files()

> for(i in matches.ipv) { # go through all matches in the file
+   cat(file=output.file, append=T,
+   whole.corpus[max(0, i-200):max(0, i-1)],
+   "\t", # print a tab stop to the file to separate the preceding context from the match
+   whole.corpus[i],
+   "\t", # print a tab stop to separate the match from the subsequent context
+   whole.corpus[(i+1):min(i+200, length(whole.corpus)+1)], # look at the words after the match
+   "\n") # the script ends the line in the output file with a new line
+ } # the script proceeds through the loop as many times as there are matches
Error in i - 200 : non-numeric argument to binary operator

As you can see, "i" is recognized as a non-numeric argument by R. Do you have an idea how I could remedy this problem?

Thanking you in advance,

C. Bechet
